name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a

name: background-bash-timeout-kills-builds
description: "A run_in_background Bash build dies at the tool timeout (ninja prints \"interrupted by user\", exit 130); launch long builds with nohup and watch the log instead"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 8c1e8dd3-1475-48e9-9398-2d5eaa424bab
  modified: 2026-09-14T19:01:34.576Z
---

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-09-23T18:10:30.736Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].

name: printer-live-harness-lessons
description: "--printer-live traps (2026-09-23): multi-line replies escape HARNESS-prefixed greps, failed runs keep a data dir holding the API key, and re-selecting a selected Bambu LAN printer deselects it"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 54c192d0-38b5-4a46-8894-652694e43240
  modified: 2026-09-23T22:16:03.023Z
---

Lessons from driving the printer chat through `--printer-live` with the live model and the fake Bambu printer:

- **A reply's later lines have no `HARNESS LIVE` prefix.** A `Choices:` line sits on its own log line, so `grep "HARNESS LIVE"` hides it. On 2026-09-23 this produced a wrong report that the model never offered choices. Grep `^Choices:` separately.
- **A failed run keeps its data dir, with the API key in it.** The harness prints `HARNESS DATA DIR kept for inspection: /var/folders/.../jusprin-shell-*`. Delete the dir your own run printed, by that path. Do not sweep every `jusprin-shell-*` holding a key: another session may be running the harness in the same checkout, and on 2026-09-23 a sweep deleted a live instance's data dir.
- **Re-selecting the selected Bambu LAN printer deselects it.** DevManager's "same lan machine" path disconnects and reconnects, and GUI_App's local-connect handler (CallAfter) then sees the lost status and calls `set_selected_machine("")` after the reconnect. The connection reports "The selected printer changed". `OrcaPrinterBackend::connect_printer` now deselects and re-selects on the next event turn. The fake printer auto-selects itself when discovered, so the first connect always hits this.
- **Close OrcaSlicer's printer list (GuideFrame) only after its page loads.** It installs its web page's script handler from a CallAfter that waits on the page; `EndModal` before the load leaves that wait hanging on a hidden view, and the app freezes with no window. On 2026-09-23 this was first blamed on the product and "fixed" with a deferral, then traced to the test and reverted. Wait for `!is_adding_script_handler()`, a non-busy page and a URL, as the old `setup_manual` check did.
- **Open the panel through `ShellController::open_printer_conversation`** in live tests; `PrinterPanel::open` skips the full-window layout.
- **The model's reliability is measured, not assumed.** gpt-5.4-mini saved changes without waiting for yes in 6 of 10 runs, even with an explicit "ask, then stop" prompt. Count across several runs before calling prompt wording fixed.

See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]].

description: "computer_batch save_to_disk produced no files (2026-09-23); to get screenshot files for a report, replay the observed host state into the built Agent/Home page under Playwright, which saves PNGs; plus the window-overlap trap when another session runs the harness."
metadata:

On 2026-09-23 a full live walkthrough of the printer panel was driven with display-scope `computer_batch` (`zoom` + `save_to_disk: true`). Every call returned the image, but no path was reported and a disk-wide search found no file. Do not count on `save_to_disk` for deliverables.

**What worked for files:** the [[fake-host-page-fixture]] recipe under the Playwright MCP. Copy `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html` (and `home/index.html`), inject `window.wx` + a `window.SCENES` table of full `state` payloads, serve with `python3 -m http.server`, open `agent.html?panel=printer`, switch scenes with `browser_evaluate` and save with `browser_take_screenshot` (`scale: device`, `filename` under the repo's `.playwright-mcp/`, the only allowed root; move the PNGs out and `rm -rf .playwright-mcp` afterwards so `git status` stays clean). Real printer pictures come from `resources/profiles/<Vendor>/<Model>_cover.png` as data URLs. The credential card renders from a `toolActivities` entry with `tool: 'printer_connect'`, `correlationId` = an assistant message id, state `pending` (card) or `succeeded` ("Sent"). Chips come from a trailing `Choices: a | b` line. 13 scenes took about 10 minutes and matched the live rendering.

**Window overlap trap:** when another session runs `JusPrinShellHarness --printer-live` in a loop, each run opens a 1200x800 window at the same origin (360,125) on the primary display and takes the front, so display-scope zooms and clicks land on *its* window. The first display click only focuses the window; click again. `--manual-live-agent` does not enable the fake Bambu printer, so the Bambu connect path is out of reach in manual mode.

**Why:** the walkthrough's evidence would otherwise have been lost, and a click into the other session's scripted run could have corrupted its result.

metadata:

When the Mac screen is locked (`ioreg -n Root -d1 | grep CGSSessionScreenIsLocked`), the computer-use MCP request is auto-denied, `screencapture` fails, and System Events sees zero windows. Return alone triggers plain "Upload" (the affirmative id), not print.

`CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` still lists the app's on-screen windows with bounds while locked, which tells you when a modal dialog is open (a small layer-0 window appears) and when it closed.

**Why:** On 2026-09-07 the end-to-end proof of the fake Moonraker printer needed the Print button pressed while the screen was locked; this was the only working path.

**How to apply:** Confirm the target pid first (`pgrep -f <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS`) so keys never go to another session's instance. name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

name: capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff
description: "How to capture the fork's wx popup menus on macOS for a pixel comparison against Windows captures, and why Windows text renders ~9% larger than the tokens intend."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 08293464-543a-44de-9266-25cac34b4e36
  modified: 2026-09-09T17:42:05.370Z
---

To compare Windows screenshots against macOS, run the same
`shell_integration_harness` fixture on both and capture each popup by window id.

**Why:** `screencapture` and any ScreenCaptureKit path fail from the Bash tool
("could not create image from display") — the Screen Recording grant belongs to a
process I cannot reach. The computer-use `app_screenshot` tool is the only route,
and it accepts a **raw CGWindowID**, not just ids from `app_list_windows`. Popups
never appear in `app_list_windows`, so enumerate them yourself.

**How to apply:**
- Build a tiny Swift lister (`CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo(.optionOnScreenOnly)`
  filtered by pid). The fork's `HeaderMenu` popups show up at `layer=101`; the main
  window is `layer=0`. Feed that id to `app_screenshot` for native-resolution pixels.
- Drive clicks with a Swift `CGEvent` helper at **global** coords
  (window origin + local). The app need not be frontmost.
- Only the **chip halves** respond to synthetic clicks. The header's overflow "…",
  the split-button chevron, and the Home back button do not — that is a limitation
  of the automation, **not** an application bug. Use the harness's own
  `--header-visual` / `--review-visual` modes for those screens instead.
- While a popup is open, the next click anywhere only dismisses it. Budget two
  clicks. Escape does not close them.
- Put the window on the **Acer H226HQL** (1920x1080, non-Retina): the harness's
  1200x800 window is then 1:1 with a Windows capture at 100% scaling, so popup
  sizes compare directly. On the built-in Retina display they would not.

**Windows text is ~9% LARGER than macOS, not smaller.** `Label::sysFont`
(`src/slic3r/GUI/Widgets/Label.cpp:19`) multiplies the point size by 4/5 off Apple
to offset Windows' 96 DPI against macOS' 72 — but 96/72 x 4/5 = 1.067, so it
under-corrects. Measured on the chip: glyph height 12 px Windows vs 11 px macOS.
Consequence: fixed-width popups ellipsize *more* on Windows. Do not assume the 4/5

---
name: capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff
description: "How to capture the fork's wx popup menus on macOS for a pixel comparison against Windows captures, and why Windows text renders ~9% larger than the tokens intend."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 08293464-543a-44de-9266-25cac34b4e36
  modified: 2026-09-09T17:42:05.370Z
---

To compare Windows screenshots against macOS, run the same
`shell_integration_harness` fixture on both and capture each popup by window id.

**Why:** `screencapture` and any ScreenCaptureKit path fail from the Bash tool
("could not create image from display") — the Screen Recording grant belongs to a
process I cannot reach. The computer-use `app_screenshot` tool is the only route,
and it accepts a **raw CGWindowID**, not just ids from `app_list_windows`. Popups
never appear in `app_list_windows`, so enumerate them yourself.

**How to apply:**
- Build a tiny Swift lister (`CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo(.optionOnScreenOnly)`
  filtered by pid). The fork's `HeaderMenu` popups show up at `layer=101`; the main
  window is `layer=0`. Feed that id to `app_screenshot` for native-resolution pixels.
- Drive clicks with a Swift `CGEvent` helper at **global** coords
  (window origin + local). The app need not be frontmost.
- Only the **chip halves** respond to synthetic clicks. The header's overflow "…",
  the split-button chevron, and the Home back button do not — that is a limitation
  of the automation, **not** an application bug. Use the harness's own
  `--header-visual` / `--review-visual` modes for those screens instead.
- While a popup is open, the next click anywhere only dismisses it. Budget two
  clicks. Escape does not close them.
- Put the window on the **Acer H226HQL** (1920x1080, non-Retina): the harness's
  1200x800 window is then 1:1 with a Windows capture at 100% scaling, so popup
  sizes compare directly. On the built-in Retina display they would not.

**Windows text is ~9% LARGER than macOS, not smaller.** `Label::sysFont`
(`src/slic3r/GUI/Widgets/Label.cpp:19`) multiplies the point size by 4/5 off Apple
to offset Windows' 96 DPI against macOS' 72 — but 96/72 x 4/5 = 1.067, so it
under-corrects. Measured on the chip: glyph height 12 px Windows vs 11 px macOS.
Consequence: fixed-width popups ellipsize *more* on Windows. Do not assume the 4/5

---
name: liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit
description: "RelWithDebInfo liblibslic3r_gui.a crossed Apple ar's 4 GiB archive limit on jusprin-newui (2026-09-13); CMAKE_AR override is ignored; manual llvm-ar relink recipe and its cd trap"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 0771473f-5d46-4419-b8e5-112938ea6b34
  modified: 2026-09-14T14:18:50.456Z
---

On 2026-09-13, at jusprin-newui 770bd2b0a2 (after "Add the evidence-led Add a
printer flow"), a worktree RelWithDebInfo build failed archiving
`src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a`:
`Assertion failed: (memberOffset < 0xFFFFFFFF) ... ArchiveWriter.cpp` then
`fatal error in .../ranlib`. The archive llvm-ar produced was 4,309,350,176
bytes; the main checkout's copy built minutes earlier was 4,143,827,796 and
still fit. Objects are big because the root CMakeLists.txt (lines ~544-548)
rewrites RelWithDebInfo -O2 to -O0 on purpose. Disk space was not the cause.

**Why:** the failed build left the OLD harness binary in place, and the harness
runs afterwards "passed" against stale code (a new `--printer-setup` flag
silently ran the default mode: same 285 check count). Gate runs on build
success and compare binary mtime.

**How to apply:**
- `-DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar` on an existing build dir does
  nothing: `CMakeFiles/<ver>/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` sets CMAKE_AR as a normal
  variable that shadows the cache.
- Working relink: `ninja -f build-RelWithDebInfo.ninja -t commands <target>`,
  drop compile lines, swap ar/ranlib for llvm-ar/llvm-ranlib on the gui archive
  line only, then run EACH line in its own `(cd build/arm64 && eval "$line")`.
  One `sh` script fails with bogus "no such file" errors because the
  encoding-check line does `cd src/slic3r` and it leaks; `sh -e` also does not
  stop inside `&&` chains. Apple's linker accepted the >4 GiB llvm-ar archive.
- The fix is PER BUILD DIRECTORY, nothing in the repo selects llvm-ar. Main
  checkout's build/arm64 cache has llvm-ar (commit 449b676145 documents it in
  agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md); any newly configured build dir
  gets Apple ar and fails again. Configure new dirs with the flags in
  [[jusprin-worktree-build]].
- Recurred 2026-09-14 on a fresh worktree at jusprin-newui bc19661a7f (archive
  4,308,513,464 bytes). Shortcut that worked: after the failed build, from
  `-t commands shell_integration_harness` drop lines containing ` -c `; only
  the last two remain relevant (gui archive, then harness link). Run just
  those two, swapping ar/ranlib on the archive line. Harness then passed.
- A lasting fix (llvm-ar in the toolchain, thin archives, or less debug info)
  is Kenneth's call; the main checkout will hit this on its next growth.

Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

entries.name: mcp__computer-use__app_ax_find
entries.description:
Search the accessibility elements captured by the last app_screenshot of one window. Filter by role (e.g. "AXTextArea", "AXButton") and/or title substring. Returns matching elements with their [N] index — pass that as element_index to app_click/app_type. Use this when the inline summary in app_screenshot doesn't show the element you need (it only lists the first few actionable ones).

This tool acts on one application in the BACKGROUND while the user keeps working in other apps. The target window does not come to the front. For the menu bar use app_menu; hover states and context menus still need the display-scope screenshot/left_click tools (which do take over the screen).

app.description: Bundle identifier of the target application (e.g. "com.apple.TextEdit"). Must be in the granted-applications list — call request_access first if it isn't.

window_id.description: CGWindowID from app_list_windows or from a previous app_screenshot result. If omitted, defaults to the window you most recently app_screenshot-ed for this app (or the app's main window if you haven't screenshotted yet). Pass a different id to switch windows — there is no separate switch-window tool; targeting is per-call via this parameter.

role.description: Exact AX role to match (e.g. "AXButton", "AXTextArea", "AXLink", "AXComboBox"). Omit to match any role.

title_contains.description: Case-insensitive substring to match against the element's title. Omit to match any title.

entries.name: mcp__computer-use__app_batch
entries.description:
Execute a sequence of app_* actions against ONE window in a single tool call. Each individual app_* call is a model→API round trip; batching a predictable sequence (e.g. click a field, type into it, press return) eliminates all but one. Actions execute sequentially and stop on the first error or 'unsupported' result. An 'ineffective' result (write accepted, app didn't visibly respond yet) does NOT stop the batch — include a screenshot action after to verify. Include {"action":"screenshot"} anywhere in the list to capture the window at that point — coordinates and element_index in actions AFTER a screenshot refer to that screenshot. Put one last to see the post-batch state in the same call.

(0, 0) is the frame's top-left corner; an app_screenshot of the window is required first. Mutually exclusive with element_index and target.

element_index.description: Index into the AX summary returned by the last app_screenshot (the [N] prefix on each line). Targets that element's center directly instead of by coordinate. Use when coordinate-based clicking returns unsupported(canvas). Mutually exclusive with coordinate and target.

Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Use for canvas-heavy apps (Pages, Keynote) where the document body has no positional accessibility elements but the app's own text cursor is somewhere editable. path.description: For drag only: [[x, y], ...] points to drag through, first = press, last = release; replaces coordinate + to_coordinate.

actions.description: e.g. [{"action":"click","coordinate":[100,200]},{"action":"type","text":"hello"},{"action":"key","combo":"return"},{"action":"screenshot"}] — type/key default to the point the previous action used.

Coordinates you write in THIS batch — clicks AND zoom regions — always refer to the full-screen screenshot taken BEFORE this call, never to a zoom and never to a mid-batch screenshot. A single action is just a one-item batch.

You declined the request for me to control the JusPrin test harness window, so I haven't clicked or typed anything in it. The harness is still running with the unchanged code, and the fix isn't written yet.

To reproduce the bug and verify the fix I need some way to act as the user. I see two options:

1. **Control the harness window in the background.** I'd use background clicks and typing, which don't take over your screen or move your cursor. You'd get the same permission prompt again, for the app `io.jusprin.shell-harness`.
2. **No screen control at all.** I'd add a harness mode that reads my prompts from a file. It would send each one to the real model as the person's message, wait for the reply, and save a screenshot of the printer panel to a PNG file after every exchange. This takes longer to build, but it runs without touching your screen, and the screenshots come out as files you can keep. The harness already has similar capture modes, such as `--timeline-capture`.

Which do you prefer? Or did you decline for another reason, for example because you were using the machine right then?

---
name: never-reuse-another-sessions-worktree
description: "A clean, merged, idle worktree under .claude/worktrees still belongs to its session; its owner can resume and check out over you mid-run. Always create your own."
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

On 2026-09-23 I reused `.claude/worktrees/compassionate-gould-f98259` to skip a full build: it was clean, detached at a commit already merged into jusprin-newui, no process had files open there, and its build dir was only 9 days old. An hour later its owning session resumed, checked out two other branches there (the reflog shows it), rewrote ~13,800 resource files, and my running harness crashed with "Could not load bitmap: bed_high_templ" -- a symptom that looked like a product bug.

**Why:** "clean and idle" says nothing about ownership. The session that created a worktree can resume at any time, and it has no way to know someone else moved in.

**How to apply:** create a new worktree with its own name (`git worktree add -b <branch> .claude/worktrees/<name> <base>`) and configure a fresh build dir with the flags in [[jusprin-worktree-build]]. At jusprin-newui bd8ea51abc a fresh build of `jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs agent_bridge_tests shell_integration_harness` was 881 ninja steps, not the hour I feared. If a harness run dies strangely, check `git -C <worktree> reflog -3 --date=iso` and file mtimes before suspecting the code. Related: [[subagent-worktrees-create-manually]].

# CLAUDE.md

OrcaSlicer — open-source C++17 3D slicer. wxWidgets GUI, CMake build system.

## Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.

# CLAUDE.md - Testing Guide for OrcaSlicer

This guide provides comprehensive instructions for Claude Code when writing, maintaining, and understanding tests in the OrcaSlicer codebase.

## ⚠️ CRITICAL RULES - MUST FOLLOW

### 1. **SECTIONS IN LOOPS - NEVER REUSE NAMES**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause unpredictable behavior
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Bad loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        SECTION("Same name") {  // WRONG! Same name used multiple times
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use DYNAMIC_SECTION or incorporate counter
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Good loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        DYNAMIC_SECTION("Section " << i) {  // Unique name per iteration
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

### 2. **THREAD SAFETY - ASSERTIONS ARE NOT THREAD-SAFE**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([]() {
            REQUIRE(some_calculation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
        });
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Synchronize results, test on main thread
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    std::atomic<int> passed{0};
    
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([&passed]() {
            if (some_calculation() == expected) {
                passed++;
            }
        });
    }
    
    for (auto& t : threads) t.join();
    REQUIRE(passed == 4);  // Test results on main thread
}
```

### 3. **EXPRESSION DECOMPOSITION - AVOID BINARY OPERATORS**
❌ **WRONG**: Cannot decompose properly
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0 && b < 10);  // Shows "false" on failure, not individual values
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Split into separate assertions
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0);
REQUIRE(b < 10);  // Each shows individual values on failure
```

### 4. **FLOATING POINT - NEVER USE APPROX**
❌ **WRONG**: Approx is deprecated and asymmetric
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_value == Catch::Approx(expected));  // Deprecated!
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use floating point matchers
```cpp
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinAbs(expected, 0.001));
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinRel(expected, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinULP(expected, 4));     // 4 ULPs apart
```

### 5. **TEST ORDERING - ALWAYS USE RANDOM ORDER**
✅ **REQUIRED**: For CI/CD and development
```bash
# Essential flags for running tests
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions

# For test sharding (parallel execution), share random seed
./tests --order rand --shard-index 0 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 1 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 2 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
```

## Overview of OrcaSlicer's Testing Framework

OrcaSlicer uses **Catch2 v3** (currently v3.11.0, vendored in `tests/catch2/`) as its primary testing framework. The test suite is organized into several modules that mirror the project's architectural components:

> **Note**: Test files include the framework via `#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>` (the v3 single-header convenience include). All v3 features described in this guide are available.

### Test Structure
```
tests/
├── CMakeLists.txt              # Main test configuration
├── catch_main.hpp              # Custom test reporter
├── libslic3r/                  # Core library tests (21 test files)
├── fff_print/                  # FFF printing tests (12 test files)
├── sla_print/                  # SLA printing tests (4 test files)
├── libnest2d/                  # 2D nesting tests
├── slic3rutils/               # Utility tests
├── data/                      # Test data files and meshes
└── catch2/                    # Catch2 framework files
```

### Build Integration
- Tests are built using CMake with `catch_discover_tests()` integration
- Each test module creates a separate executable (e.g., `libslic3r_tests`, `fff_print_tests`)
- Test data directory is available via `TEST_DATA_DIR` preprocessor definition
- Custom verbose console reporter provides detailed test output

## Test Suite Organization

### libslic3r Tests
Core slicing engine tests covering:
- **Geometry operations**: Points, polygons, lines, Voronoi diagrams
- **File formats**: STL, 3MF, AMF parsing and validation
- **Algorithms**: Clipper operations, mesh boolean operations, optimization
- **Configuration**: Print settings validation and parsing
- **Utilities**: String processing, time utilities, data structures

### fff_print Tests
Fused Filament Fabrication specific tests:
- **G-code generation**: Writer functionality, cooling, lift/unlift
- **Slicing algorithms**: Layer generation, infill patterns
- **Print mechanics**: Flow calculations, extrusion, support material
- **Model processing**: Print objects, skirt/brim generation

### sla_print Tests
Stereolithography specific tests:
- **SLA print processing**: Layer curing, support generation
- **Raycast operations**: Light path calculations
- **Test utilities**: SLA-specific helper functions

## Writing New Tests - Best Practices

### File Organization
1. **Naming Convention**: `test_<feature>.cpp` (e.g., `test_geometry.cpp`)
2. **Header Structure**: Include `<catch2/catch_all.hpp>` first, then relevant headers
3. **Namespace Usage**: Use `using namespace Slic3r;` for convenience
4. **File Placement**: Add to appropriate test directory and update CMakeLists.txt

### Test Naming and Structure
```cpp
#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>
#include "libslic3r/Point.hpp"

using namespace Slic3r;

TEST_CASE("Feature description", "[category_tag]") {
    // Test implementation
}
```

### Tagging System
Use descriptive tags for test categorization:
- `[Geometry]` - Geometric operations and calculations
- `[GCodeWriter]` - G-code generation functionality  
- `[Config]` - Configuration and settings tests
- `[FileFormat]` - File I/O operations (STL, 3MF, etc.)
- `[Algorithm]` - Core algorithms and processing
- `[Performance]` - Performance benchmarks (if applicable)

## Catch2 Features Guide

### Basic Assertions
```cpp
// Primary assertions - stop test on failure
REQUIRE(expression);
REQUIRE_FALSE(expression);

// Continuing assertions - continue test after failure  
CHECK(expression);
CHECK_FALSE(expression);

// Non-failing checks - record result but don't fail test
CHECK_NOFAIL(expression);  // Useful for assumptions that might be violated
```

### Exception Testing
```cpp
// Verify no exception is thrown
REQUIRE_NOTHROW(function_call());

// Verify any exception is thrown
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());

// Verify specific exception type
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(function_call(), SpecificException);

// Verify exception message
REQUIRE_THROWS_WITH(function_call(), "Expected error message");

// Verify exception with matchers (for partial matching)
REQUIRE_THROWS_MATCHES(function_call(), SpecificException, 
                       Catch::Matchers::Message("contains this"));
```

### Complex Assertions with Matchers
```cpp
#include <catch2/matchers/catch_matchers.hpp>

// String matchers
using Catch::Matchers::StartsWith;
using Catch::Matchers::EndsWith;
using Catch::Matchers::ContainsSubstring;
using Catch::Matchers::Equals;
using Catch::Matchers::Matches;  // Regex matching

REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, StartsWith("Expected prefix"));
REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, ContainsSubstring("middle part"));
REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, Matches(".*pattern.*"));

// Floating point matchers - ALWAYS use these instead of Approx!
using Catch::Matchers::WithinAbs;
using Catch::Matchers::WithinRel;
using Catch::Matchers::WithinULP;

REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinAbs(expected, 0.001));     // Absolute tolerance
REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinRel(expected, 0.01));      // Relative tolerance (1%)
REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinULP(expected, 4));         // ULP difference (requires IEEE-754)

// Combining matchers
REQUIRE_THAT(value, WithinRel(expected, 0.001) || WithinAbs(0.0, 0.000001));
```

### Sections for Test Organization
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Complex feature testing", "[Feature]") {
    // Common setup code
    SomeObject obj;
    
    SECTION("First scenario") {
        // Specific test case
        REQUIRE(obj.method1() == expected_value);
    }
    
    SECTION("Second scenario") {
        // Another test case with same setup
        REQUIRE(obj.method2() == other_expected);
    }
}
```

### BDD-Style Tests
Use for complex scenarios and user story testing:

> **Note**: BDD macros are aliases for TEST_CASE and SECTION with prefixed names
```cpp
SCENARIO("User performs complex operation", "[UserStory]") {
    GIVEN("A specific setup condition") {
        GCodeWriter writer;
        // Setup code
        
        WHEN("User performs action") {
            auto result = writer.some_operation();
            
            THEN("Expected outcome occurs") {
                REQUIRE(result.size() > 0);
                
                AND_WHEN("Follow-up action occurs") {
                    auto next_result = writer.next_operation();
                    
                    THEN("Final outcome is correct") {
                        REQUIRE(next_result == expected);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

### Data Generators for Parameterized Tests
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Function works with various inputs", "[Algorithm]") {
    auto test_value = GENERATE(1, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13);
    
    REQUIRE(is_odd(test_value));
    REQUIRE(test_value > 0);
}

// Range-based generators
TEST_CASE("Range testing", "[Algorithm]") {
    auto i = GENERATE(range(1, 10));  // 1 to 9
    REQUIRE(process_value(i) > i);
}

// Using variables in generators (requires GENERATE_COPY or GENERATE_REF)
TEST_CASE("Generator with variables", "[Algorithm]") {
    std::vector<int> values = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5};
    auto test_value = GENERATE_REF(from_range(values));  // Use GENERATE_REF for references
    
    REQUIRE(test_value > 0);
}

// Custom generators
TEST_CASE("Random values", "[Algorithm]") {
    auto random_int = GENERATE(take(100, random(-1000, 1000)));  // 100 random values
    REQUIRE(process_random_value(random_int));
}
```

### Test Fixtures
```cpp
class GeometryFixture {
public:
    Point origin{0, 0};
    Point unit_x{1, 0};
    Point unit_y{0, 1};
    
    mutable double tolerance = EPSILON;  // Use mutable for data that might change
};

// Standard fixture - new instance per test run
TEST_CASE_METHOD(GeometryFixture, "Point operations", "[Geometry]") {
    REQUIRE(origin.distance_to(unit_x) == 1.0);
}

// Persistent fixture - single instance for entire test case (v3.2.0+)
TEST_CASE_PERSISTENT_FIXTURE(GeometryFixture, "Persistent operations", "[Geometry]") {
    static int call_count = 0;
    ++call_count;
    INFO("This fixture persists across sections, call: " << call_count);
    
    SECTION("First section") {
        REQUIRE(origin.distance_to(unit_x) == 1.0);
    }
    
    SECTION("Second section") {
        REQUIRE(origin.distance_to(unit_y) == 1.0);
        // call_count will be 2 here with persistent fixture
    }
}

// Template fixtures for type-parameterized tests
template<typename T>
class NumericFixture {
public:
    T zero = T{0};
    T one = T{1};
};

TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE_METHOD(NumericFixture, "Numeric operations", "[Template]", int, float, double) {
    REQUIRE(TestType{} == this->zero);
    REQUIRE(TestType{1} == this->one);
}
```

### Advanced Testing Features

#### Logging and Information Macros
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Advanced logging", "[Logging]") {
    INFO("This info persists until end of scope");
    
    SECTION("Section A") {
        INFO("Section A specific info");
        CAPTURE(some_variable, another_var);  // Captures variable names and values
        CHECK(some_condition);
    }
    
    SECTION("Section B") {
        UNSCOPED_INFO("This survives beyond its scope");  // v2.7.0+
        CHECK(other_condition);
    }
}

// Warning and explicit control
TEST_CASE("Explicit test control", "[Control]") {
    WARN("This warns but doesn't fail the test");
    
    if (precondition_not_met) {
        SKIP("Reason");  // Marks the test as skipped (v3.3.0+, available)
        return;
    }
    
    if (critical_failure) {
        FAIL("Critical condition failed");  // Fails and stops test
    }
    
    SUCCEED("Reached successful completion");  // Explicit success marker
}
```

```cpp
TEST_CASE("Compile-time checks", "[Static]") {
    STATIC_REQUIRE(sizeof(int) >= 4);  // Checked at compile time
    STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE(std::is_void_v<int>);
    
    // For traits and template metaprogramming
    STATIC_CHECK(std::is_trivially_copyable_v<Point>);  // v3.0.1+

```

#### Conditional Testing
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Conditional blocks", "[Conditional]") {
    int value = get_test_value();
    
    // These record the expression but don't count as test failures (v3.0.1+)
    CHECKED_IF(value > 0) {
        // This block runs if value > 0
        REQUIRE(value <= 100);
    } CHECKED_ELSE(value > 0) {
        // This block runs if value <= 0

}
```

```cpp
TEST_CASE("Performance testing", "[Benchmark]") {
    // Simple benchmarking
    BENCHMARK("Algorithm performance") {
        return expensive_algorithm();
    };
    
    // Advanced benchmarking with setup
    BENCHMARK_ADVANCED("Advanced benchmark")(Catch::Benchmark::Chronometer meter) {
        std::vector<int> data = setup_test_data();  // Setup not measured
        
        meter.measure([&] { 
            return process_data(data);  // Only this is measured
        });
    };
}
```

## OrcaSlicer-Specific Testing Patterns

### Geometry Testing
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Line operations", "[Geometry]") {
    Line line{{100000, 0}, {0, 0}};
    Line parallel{{200000, 0}, {0, 0}};
    
    REQUIRE(line.parallel_to(line));
    REQUIRE(line.parallel_to(parallel));
```

```cpp
TEST_CASE("Config loading", "[Config]") {
    DynamicPrintConfig config;
```

```cpp
TEST_CASE("STL file parsing", "[FileFormat]") {
    std::string stl_path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/test_stl/20mmbox.stl";
```

```cpp
TEST_CASE("G-code writer functionality", "[GCodeWriter]") {
    GCodeWriter writer;
    
    // Load test configuration
    std::string config_path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/fff_print_tests/test_config.ini";
    writer.config.load(config_path, ForwardCompatibilitySubstitutionRule::Disable);
```

```cpp
TEST_CASE("Algorithm performance", "[Performance][Algorithm]") {
    // Large test data
    std::vector<Point> points = generate_large_point_set(10000);
    
    // Time the operation (manual timing example; the BENCHMARK macro is also available)
    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
```

#### For Custom Types
```cpp
// Method 1: operator<< overload (preferred)
std::ostream& operator<<(std::ostream& os, const Point& point) {
    os << "Point(" << point.x << ", " << point.y << ")";
    return os;
}

// Method 2: StringMaker specialization
```

## Common Pitfalls and Solutions

### Floating-Point Comparisons

> **CRITICAL**: Never use Approx - it's deprecated due to asymmetry and other issues

❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == expected_volume);           // Exact equality
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == Catch::Approx(expected));   // Deprecated! Asymmetric!
```

✅ **Correct**: Always use floating point matchers
```cpp
// Absolute tolerance - good when values are near zero
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinAbs(expected_volume, 0.001));

// Relative tolerance - good for values with different magnitudes
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance

// ULP (Units in Last Place) - most precise, requires IEEE-754
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinULP(expected_volume, 4));

// Combined approach - relative OR absolute
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, 
    WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.001) || WithinAbs(0.0, 0.000001));

// Precision control for output
Catch::StringMaker<double>::precision = 15;  // Show more decimal places
```

### Why Approx is Problematic:
- **Asymmetric**: `Approx(10).epsilon(0.1) != 11.1` but `Approx(11.1).epsilon(0.1) == 10`
- **Double-only**: All computation done in `double`, causes issues with `float` inputs  
- **Default behavior**: Only uses relative comparison, so `Approx(0) == X` only works for `X == 0`

### Path Handling
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
std::string path = TEST_DATA_DIR + "/model.obj";  // May have path separator issues
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
std::string path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/model.obj";
// or use boost::filesystem for complex path operations
```

### Exception Testing
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
bool threw_exception = false;
try {
    risky_function();
} catch (...) {
    threw_exception = true;
}
REQUIRE(threw_exception);
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());
// or for specific exceptions
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(risky_function(), SpecificException);
```

### Thread Safety

⚠️ **CRITICAL**: Catch2 assertions are **NOT thread-safe** by default!

> **Note**: Catch2 v3.9.0+ has opt-in thread-safe assertions via `CATCH_CONFIG_EXPERIMENTAL_THREAD_SAFE_ASSERTIONS`. OrcaSlicer is on v3.11.0 but does not enable this flag, so assertions remain non-thread-safe by default.

❌ **Incorrect**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
std::thread t([&]() {
    REQUIRE(threaded_operation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
    CHECK(other_operation());                   // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
});
```

✅ **Correct**: Collect results, assert on main thread
```cpp
std::atomic<bool> success{false};
std::atomic<int> error_count{0};

std::thread t([&]() {
    // Do work in thread, collect results
    bool result1 = (threaded_operation() == expected);
    bool result2 = other_operation();
    
    if (result1 && result2) {
        success = true;
    } else {
        error_count++;
    }
});

t.join();

// Assert results on main thread
REQUIRE(success);
REQUIRE(error_count == 0);
```

#### Thread Safety Rules:
- **REQUIRE family**: Would terminate process in spawned threads (throws exception with no try-catch)
- **CHECK family**: Not thread-safe, can corrupt internal state
- **SKIP, FAIL, SUCCEED**: Not thread-safe even with v3 thread-safe assertions
- **Message macros**: INFO, CAPTURE, WARN - not thread-safe
- **STATIC_REQUIRE/CHECK**: Not thread-safe (relies on runtime registration)

### Memory Management
Use RAII and smart pointers in tests:
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Resource management", "[Memory]") {
    auto model = std::make_unique<Model>();
    // Automatic cleanup on test completion/failure
    
    REQUIRE(model->objects.empty());
}
```

```cpp
TEST_CASE("Performance-sensitive test", "[Performance]") {
```

### Platform-Specific Issues

entries.name: PushNotification
entries.description:
This tool sends a desktop notification in the user's terminal. If Remote Control is connected, it also pushes to their phone. Either way, it pulls their attention from whatever they're doing — a meeting, another task, dinner — to this session. That's the cost. The benefit is they learn something now that they'd want to know now: a long task finished while they were away, a build is ready, you've hit something that needs their decision before you can continue.

Because a notification they didn't need is annoying in a way that accumulates, err toward not sending one. Don't notify for routine progress, or to announce you've answered something they asked seconds ago and are clearly still watching, or when a quick task completes. Notify when there's a real chance they've walked away and there's something worth coming back for — or when they've explicitly asked you to notify them.

Keep the message under 200 characters, one line, no markdown. Lead with what they'd act on — "build failed: 2 auth tests" tells them more than "task done" and more than a status dump.

When the user is actively at the terminal, your output already reaches them — a notification on top of it would be a duplicate, so the tool skips it and says so. A "not sent" result is expected and only ever about this one notification: it was redundant, turned off, or had nowhere to go.

content.text:
The false connection block is fixed and verified live, but not committed. On the unchanged code it appeared in 2 of 3 realistic conversations. After the fix it didn't appear in any of 4, including 2 where the model made the same bad call. The eight screenshots are attached.

**What the bug actually was.** When a user asked to connect before giving an address, the model sometimes called `printer_connect` with incomplete arguments: `{"address":""}` or `{"hostType":"moonraker"}`. The app refused those calls before showing a card, but the thread still showed a "Connect this printer · Sent" block, and only then did the model ask for the address. The walkthrough's version, where the printer's name was used as the address, didn't come up in any of my 7 runs.

**Live results.** I captured each call's exact arguments through a local logging proxy between the app and OpenAI.

| Run | Printer and what the user typed | `printer_connect` call | What the user saw |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before 1 | K1 Max, "can you hook it up so i can send prints to it from here?" | `{"address":""}` | "Connect this printer · Sent" |
| Before 2 | SV08, "Yes", then "no idea what the address is… can't you just find it?" | none | a question, no block |
| Before 3 | Neptune 4 Pro, "yes please go ahead" | `{"hostType":"moonraker"}` | "Connect this printer · Sent" |
| After 1 | K1 Max, same words as Before 1 | `{"hostType":"moonraker"}`, refused | a question only; the card appeared after "i think its 192.168.1.87" |
| After 2 | Neptune 4 Pro, "just connect it please, it's on the same wifi as my mac" | none | a question only |
| After 3 | Qidi X-Plus 4, "great, now connect it" | `{"hostType":"moonraker"}`, refused | a question only |
| After 4 | Qidi, from the card menu's "Connect…", then "idk, can you just try?" | none | a question only |

**What changed** (branch `claude/printer-connect-card-facets` in `.claude/worktrees/printer-connect-card-facets`):
- [ToolRegistry.cpp](.claude/worktrees/printer-connect-card-facets/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp): `printer_connect` now accepts exactly one of two argument sets: a non-empty `deviceId` alone, or `hostType` with a non-empty `address`. Anything else is refused before an activity exists, so nothing is drawn in the thread. As you asked, there is no address-shape check and no check that the person typed the address.
- The refused call gets a specific hint telling the model to ask the person for the address and call again once they give it. The tool's schema descriptions state the same rule.
- [PrinterConversation.cpp](.claude/worktrees/printer-connect-card-facets/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp): the pre-card check no longer re-tests for an empty address, since the argument check now guarantees one. It still refuses a Bambu `deviceId` sent for a Moonraker or OctoPrint printer.
- [test_printer_conversation.cpp](.claude/worktrees/printer-connect-card-facets/tests/agent/test_printer_conversation.cpp): a new test using the exact calls from the live runs. It failed on the old code and passes now, and all 248 agent test cases pass.

**Still open:**
- **Other refusals still show "Sent".** Any call the pre-card check refuses is still drawn as "… · Sent". Examples: a Bambu `deviceId` sent for a Moonraker printer, an unknown Bambu device, or a printer whose connection type isn't supported. That label comes from `PrinterPanel.tsx:79` and is walkthrough section 3's problem.
- **Name-as-address isn't blocked.** A call with the printer's name as the address, like `{"hostType":"moonraker","address":"Creality K1"}`, still passes, because of your decision on the shape check.
- **The Bambu path was only unit-tested.** The manual harness can't start the fake Bambu printer, so I didn't exercise it live.
- **Another session's test may have been affected.** When another session's scripted test (`--printer-connect-trials 10`) opened its window over mine, one click and the text "sovol sv08" may have landed in one of its trials. Its thread didn't show the message, but one trial could be affected.

Do you want me to commit this?

content.text:
**Summary:** the fix works in my tests. Before it, the bug showed up in 2 of 3 test conversations. After it, the bug didn't show up in any of 4. Nothing is committed yet.

**What was wrong**

A user adds a printer, then asks the assistant to connect it without saying the printer's network address. Sometimes the assistant tries to connect anyway. The app correctly refuses, because there's nothing to connect to. But the chat still showed a box saying "Connect this printer · Sent", which tells the user something was sent when nothing was. After that box, the assistant asked for the address it should have asked for first.

**How I tested it**

I ran the app and typed the way a new user would, with a different printer and different wording each time. I also recorded exactly what the assistant tried to do behind the scenes, so I could see when it attempted a connection without an address.

**Before the fix (3 conversations):**

1. Creality K1 Max. I typed "can you hook it up so i can send prints to it from here?" The assistant tried to connect with no address. **The false "Sent" box appeared.**
2. Sovol SV08. I tapped "Yes" to connect, then typed "no idea what the address is… can't you just find it?" The assistant didn't try to connect; it asked for the address. No false box.
3. Elegoo Neptune 4 Pro. I typed "yes please go ahead". The assistant tried to connect with no address. **The false "Sent" box appeared.**

**After the fix (4 conversations):**

1. Creality K1 Max, same words as before. The assistant again tried to connect with no address. **This time the app stopped it quietly, no box appeared, and the assistant simply asked for the address.** When I typed "i think its 192.168.1.87", the real connection form appeared, as it should.
2. Elegoo Neptune 4 Pro. I typed "just connect it please, it's on the same wifi as my mac". The assistant asked for the address. No box.
3. Qidi X-Plus 4. I typed "great, now connect it". The assistant tried to connect with no address. **The app stopped it, no box appeared, and the assistant asked for the address.**
4. Qidi X-Plus 4 again, this time starting from the printer's "Connect…" menu on the home screen. I typed "idk, can you just try?" The assistant asked for the address. No box.

The screenshots I sent show these conversations.

**What I changed**

- The app now refuses a connection attempt early unless it has either the ID of a Bambu printer found on the network, or both the printer type and an address. Refusing that early means nothing is shown in the chat.
- When the app refuses, it tells the assistant to ask the person for the address, and I added the same instruction to the assistant's description of the connect action.
- I added an automated test with the exact bad attempts from my runs. It failed before the fix and passes now, and all the other existing tests still pass.

**What is still not fixed**

- The app still shows "Sent" for other refused connection attempts. For example, the assistant might use the wrong kind of printer ID, or the printer might use a connection type the app doesn't support. That label problem is item 3 in the walkthrough.
- If the assistant uses the printer's name as the address, such as "Creality K1", the connection form still appears. That's because you decided against checking what the address looks like. It didn't happen in any of my 7 conversations.
- I couldn't test Bambu printers by hand, because the test app I used can't simulate one. Only the automated test covers them.
- Another session was running its own automatic test at the same time, and its window once covered mine. One of my clicks and the text "sovol sv08" may have gone into its window, which could have affected one of its test rounds.

Do you want me to commit this?

"Connect this printer · Sent". The person saw a claim that something was
sent, and only then was asked for the address.

The registry's decoder now accepts exactly one of two argument sets: a
non-empty deviceId alone (Bambu Lab), or hostType with a non-empty
address (Moonraker or OctoPrint). A call the decoder refuses goes back
to the model as an error and never becomes an activity, so nothing is
drawn. The refusal and the schema descriptions tell the model to ask
for the address instead. The panel's check keeps only what the decoder
cannot know: a deviceId sent for a printer that is not a Bambu Lab one.

Verified live with the shell harness and the real model, typing as a
new user, with every call's arguments recorded through a local proxy:
before the change the false "Sent" block appeared in 2 of 3
conversations; after it, 0 of 4, including 2 where the model made the
same incomplete call and then asked for the address. Giving an address
still shows the credential card. agent_bridge_tests: 248 test cases
pass; the new test fails on the old decoder.

Not covered: other refusals from the panel's check (a wrong kind of
device id, an unsupported connection type) are still drawn as "Sent",
